android.extraProguardRules:
# Mufify. R8 runs in full mode and these are the only things it cannot see.
#
# Deliberately short. Expo and React Native ship consumer rules that already
# cover everything reached by reflection in their own worlds — anything
# extending `expo.modules.kotlin.modules.Module`, implementing `Record` or
# `Enumerable`, or annotated `@DoNotStrip` — and that includes every module
# under `dev.mufify`. A blanket keep on our own packages would have cost most
# of the obfuscation for nothing.

# Nitro's C++ side finds these across JNI, by name. react-native-mmkv is a
# Nitro module, MMKV holds every setting, and the theme is read from it
# before the first frame — so this failing is a blank app, not a lost value.
-keep class com.margelo.nitro.** { *; }

# `@Keep` is androidx's, and react-native-mmkv marks its JNI entry points
# with Fresco's `DoNotStrip` rather than the one React Native's own rules
# name. Neither is covered by the default file this build uses.
-keep @androidx.annotation.Keep class * { *; }
-keepclassmembers class * { @androidx.annotation.Keep *; }
-keep @com.facebook.common.internal.DoNotStrip class * { *; }
-keepclassmembers class * { @com.facebook.common.internal.DoNotStrip *; }

# Exception class names, so a failure that reaches the user still says what
# it was: `TagReader` falls back to the simple name when there is no message,
# and "a" is not a thing anyone can report.
-keepnames class * extends java.lang.Throwable
